title: fix(console-starter): namespace a spec translation payload the way the console does
body:
Fixes #10349
Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`examples/console-starter/src/main.tsx` handed `I18nProvider` a `loadLanguage` that ended `return json?.data?.translations ?? json ?? {};`. The server answers `/api/v1/i18n/translations/:lang` with a spec `TranslationData` document, so the starter put that document at the root of the i18next resource tree. `useObjectLabel` only discovers app namespaces one level down (`getAppNamespaces`). An author starting from the template therefore saw their source labels in every locale, with no error. The reference console (`apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts`) branches on `isSpecTranslationData` and sends a spec payload through `transformSpecTranslations`, which namespaces it under `app`.

## What changed

- `examples/console-starter/src/loadLanguage.ts` (new) holds the starter's loader, moved out of `main.tsx` so a test can import it without mounting the app (`main.tsx` renders into `#root` at import time).
  - Its last step is now the console's branch, `isSpecTranslationData(translations) ? transformSpecTranslations(translations) : translations`. Both functions are imported from `@object-ui/i18n`, and no copy of the transform lives in the example.
  - Everything else is as it was: the same URL, the same envelope unwrap (`json?.data?.translations ?? json ?? {}`), and the same `{}` on an HTTP error or a throw.
- `examples/console-starter/src/main.tsx` imports `loadLanguage` from `./loadLanguage` and wires it into `I18nProvider` exactly as before.
- `examples/console-starter/test/loadLanguage.test.tsx` (new) has eight tests. Each goes through the real loader with a stubbed `fetch`:
  - (a) The card's payload carries an object label and a field label. It comes out as `{ app: { objects: { crm_lead: { label: '线索' } }, fields: { crm_lead: { name: '名称' } } } }`. That result is handed to i18next with the `addResourceBundle` call `I18nProvider` makes, and `useObjectLabel` then renders `线索` and `名称`, not `Lead` and `Name`.
  - (b) Controls: an app-namespaced tree inside the envelope, and a built-in override with no envelope, both come back unchanged.
  - (c) Controls: an empty translations document, a null body, an HTTP 500 and a thrown fetch each yield `{}`.
- `examples/console-starter/README.md`: the sentence on translation loading now names `src/loadLanguage.ts`. It says a spec payload is namespaced with `transformSpecTranslations`, and an already-namespaced tree passes through.

This is the same defect class as objectui#10235, which PR objectui#10344 addressed on the console side. The new test follows the shape of `apps/console/src/loadLanguage.test.tsx`.

## Premise and mechanism assumptions, measured on `origin/main` `6096f20b3`

- **Premise holds.** `main.tsx`'s `loadLanguage` ended in the bare `return json?.data?.translations ?? json ?? {};` and imported neither function.
- **No dependency change needed.** `@object-ui/example-console-starter` already depends on `@object-ui/i18n` (`workspace:*`), and `vite.config.ts` already aliases it, so `package.json` is untouched. `test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts` walks the new module and stays green.
- **The test is wired.**
  - The starter's `test` script points at the root config. That config's `dom` project includes `examples/**/*.test.tsx` and aliases `@object-ui/i18n` to its source.
  - `tsconfig.test.json` includes `test/**/*.test.tsx`, so the new test is type-checked too.
- **No changeset.** The package is private. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` reports: 4 files changed, 0 of them published source of a package the release covers, so no changeset is owed. None is added.
- **Left alone.** The console loader does two things this one still does not. This card needs only the branch.
  - It calls `console.warn` on an HTTP error and on a throw.
  - It takes `data.translations` only when it is an object. The starter's `??` chain also accepts a non-object value there.

## Evidence (every run at `3952046ed`)

- **Tests.** `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --reporter=verbose examples/console-starter/` ran from the repo root, through the verify lock: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 17 passed (17)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The 17 are the 8 new tests plus the 9 alias-closure tests.
- **Ablation**, run with `ablation-replace.mjs` after the fix was committed at `2c48e2f9a`.
  - Mutation: the loader's return reverted to the bare `return json?.data?.translations ?? json ?? {};`. The anchor count went from 1 to 0, the replacement count from 0 to 1, and the blob from `9dbe6072efdf` to `09ca58e2c1b3`.
  - Result: **2 red, 6 green**, as predicted. Both (a) pins went red:
    - `expected { objects: { crm_lead: { …(2) } } } to deeply equal { app: { objects: { …(1) }, …(1) } }`;
    - `expected 'Lead' to be '线索'`, which is the card's probe.
  - The six (b) and (c) controls stayed green. They pin the branch that did not change.
  - Restore: the blob is back to `9dbe6072efdf` (equal to HEAD) and `git diff HEAD` is empty. Re-checked by hand: anchor count 1, bare-return count 0.
- **Type check.**
  - First the dependency closure was built: `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/example-console-starter^...`, 29 of 29 tasks.
  - Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/example-console-starter type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0.
  - `--listFiles` shows `tsconfig.json` compiles `src/main.tsx` and `src/loadLanguage.ts`, and `tsconfig.test.json` compiles `test/loadLanguage.test.tsx`.
- **Gates**, all exit 0:
  - `check:control-bytes`;
  - `check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`);
  - `check-changeset-presence` (no changeset owed);
  - `check:changeset-claims`, which read nothing here because this change has no changeset;
  - `check-doc-links` (`Links are valid across 17 scan roots`; `examples/**` is a scan root);
  - `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-type-check-coverage` and `check:esm-specifiers`.
- **Lint, narrowed to the touched files.**
  - Scope: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the three touched `.ts`/`.tsx` files. None of them is ignored by `eslint.config.js`, and the JSON reports 3 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
  - Why the narrowing holds: `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem. So this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **End to end through `I18nProvider`'s own `loadLanguage` prop, the path `main.tsx` uses, the translation shows only on the consumer's next render.** The fix gets the bundle into i18next correctly. An uncommitted probe mounted `I18nProvider loadLanguage={loadLanguage}` in zh-CN over the card's payload and read the following:
  - the loader was called once, with `zh-CN`;
  - the resource bundle carried the right `app` namespace;
  - the consumer had rendered once, and it still read `Lead`;
  - after one forced state bump, it read `线索`.

  After `addResourceBundle`, the provider's "Force re-render" step is `setLanguage(currentLang)` with the language it already holds, so React skips the update. That code is in `packages/i18n`, outside this claim, and the console is wired the same way. It is reported to the seat, not changed here. The pins above measure the loader and the reader, which is this card's defect.

Implemented by the dispatched `os-dev` run for seat `domain:ui#1`, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`.
